v.why: When edge 5 already supplies a learned conv into node 3, a parallel conv on edge 4 is partly redundant, giving diminishing returns.
Node 2 already receives convolved features via edge 2, so a second conv on edge 1 is partly redundant.
When sibling edge 4 has no parameters, edge 5 must supply the output's learned features, so a conv there is worth more.
With edge 4 a skip, node 1's features go straight to the output, so edge 0's conv is the only learned stage on that path and matters more.
A skip on edge 3 forms a residual block around the conv branch through edge 4, improving gradient flow.
Adding a conv mid-path lengthens the longest chain, which trains better with an identity bypass on edge 3.
A skip after a skip makes node 2 partly an identity copy of the input, collapsing effective depth.
Serial skips along 1->2->3 strip learned computation from the deepest path, a compounding loss of depth.
Without the direct shortcut the output depends more on edge 5, so pooling there hurts more.
With edge 5 removed, fewer routes reach the output, so a clean shortcut on edge 3 is more valuable for signal and gradient flow.
